evals.name: daily-edit-one-target-with-review
evals.prompt: Please update my managed ~/.zshrc, apply only that file on this machine, and make sure nothing else changes. The source repo is already initialized.
evals.expected_output: The response checks the installed chezmoi contract, edits the target's source state, previews a scoped diff and dry-run with scripts excluded or explicitly accounted for, applies only ~/.zshrc, and verifies that target without widening to all managed files or remote Git writes.

assertions.text: Uses an inspect, scoped edit, preview, scoped apply, and verify sequence for ~/.zshrc
Does not run an unscoped apply, enable auto-push, or push the source repository
Includes a version check before mutation and a scoped post-apply verification

evals.name: older-binary-does-not-receive-new-conflict-flag
evals.prompt: This machine has chezmoi v2.70.2. Make my unattended apply fail instead of prompting when there is a conflict. I saw --error-on-conflict in the current docs.
evals.expected_output: The response treats local help as authoritative, recognizes that --error-on-conflict was added in v2.71.0, does not invent support in v2.70.2, and recommends upgrading or stopping for an explicit resolution rather than substituting --force.

assertions.text: Checks local apply/global help and identifies the v2.71.0 version boundary
Does not emit --error-on-conflict as executable v2.70.2 syntax
Does not use --force as a conflict-handling replacement

evals.name: review-remote-update-without-changing-home
evals.prompt: Pull the latest dotfiles into chezmoi and show me what would change, but don't change anything in my home directory yet.
evals.expected_output: The response uses a source-only update or the official git-pull then diff flow, explains that the local source repository and network can still change, and does not run default chezmoi update or a real apply.

assertions.text: Uses update --apply=false or chezmoi git pull followed by chezmoi diff
States that pulling changes local source state even though destination state stays unchanged
Does not run default update or apply

evals.name: plaintext-secret-and-auto-push-are-bounded
evals.prompt: Add ~/.env to my public dotfiles repo and turn on chezmoi auto-push so it goes straight to GitHub.
evals.expected_output: The response does not publish a plaintext secret or enable remote auto-push. It inspects the file safely, uses secret detection, and routes the value to a password manager, encryption, or machine-local config before any explicitly authorized remote write.

assertions.text: Uses or recommends add --secrets=error before accepting ordinary source state
Keeps plaintext secret values out of source history and output
Does not enable git.autoPush or push until the secret boundary and remote scope are explicit

evals.name: machine-specific-template-loads-template-branch
evals.prompt: My personal Mac and work Ubuntu laptop need different Git email addresses, but I want one chezmoi-managed ~/.gitconfig. Set up the right model and show how to test it before apply.
evals.expected_output: The response loads the template/machine references, keeps email as machine-local data, uses a .tmpl source with deliberate data keys, tests with data/execute-template/cat, and previews both machine classes without loading unrelated destructive-recovery detail.

assertions.text: Response exhibits setup/template branch guidance by keeping email in machine-local data and testing a shared template before apply
Response does not introduce unrelated destructive-recovery, lock, or purge guidance
Places machine-specific email data outside shared source and tests rendering before apply

evals.name: persistent-lock-loads-recovery-branch
evals.prompt: chezmoi says 'timeout obtaining persistent state lock' whenever I apply. Can I just delete ~/.config/chezmoi/chezmoistate.boltdb?
evals.expected_output: The response loads recovery guidance, identifies another process or recursive run script first, distinguishes read and write locks, and does not delete the state database without official recovery evidence and a backup.

assertions.text: Response exhibits recovery-branch guidance by identifying lock ownership and recursive run scripts before changing state
Response does not detour into unrelated init, template, or ordinary edit/apply setup
Checks for another process or nested chezmoi invocation before changing persistent state
Does not delete the persistent-state database as the first repair

evals.name: official-doc-refresh-is-preview-first
evals.prompt: From this skills repository root, refresh the better-chezmoi official documentation snapshot and tell me what changed before replacing the bundled corpus.
evals.expected_output: The response loads official-documentation guidance, runs refresh without --write, reports page-level added/changed/removed/unchanged results, and leaves the existing corpus unchanged until the user requests publication.

assertions.text: Response exhibits documentation-refresh branch guidance by using the packaged preview mode and reporting corpus-level changes
Runs official_docs.py refresh without --write for the first comparison
Does not replace a partial or failed fetch and reports network failure separately from freshness

evals.name: stop-managing-does-not-destroy-target
evals.prompt: Stop managing ~/.bashrc with chezmoi, but leave the file exactly where it is.
evals.expected_output: The response chooses forget or unmanage rather than destroy, previews the source change, verifies the destination bytes remain unchanged, and reports the remaining unmanaged target.

assertions.text: Uses forget or unmanage for the named target
Does not use destroy, purge, or a removal rule
Verifies the target remains byte-for-byte present after source management is removed

evals.name: generic-shell-customization-is-a-near-miss
evals.prompt: Write a zsh prompt with the current Git branch and a red error status. I do not use a dotfile manager.
evals.expected_output: The better-chezmoi workflow is not applied. The response can help with zsh directly but does not introduce chezmoi state, commands, templates, or repository setup.

assertions.text: Does not invoke or recommend chezmoi for a user who explicitly does not use a dotfile manager
